newsitem.title: USA: Keithley to consolidate, take Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Keithley to consolidate, take Q4 charge.

text.p: Keithley Instruments Inc said on Thursday that it would take a $10 million, or $1.12 per share, after-tax charge in the fourth quarter for the relocation and consolidation of some of its businesses.
The company said in a statement that it would relocate its MetraByte operations to Cleveland from Taunton, Mass. and form a new Data Acquisition Business.
Keithley said the $10 million charge included a non-cash write-off of $5.7 million, or $0.73, after tax for remaining intangibles associated with the 1989 MetraByte acquisition.
The rest of the charge would be for personnel reductions and other relocation expenses, it said.

"We expect the Taunton operation, which has 121 employees, to be transitioned to Cleveland over the next six to nine months," Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Joseph Keithley said in a statement. "Because of expected manufacturing and operational efficiencies, Cleveland employment will not grow equivalently."
The company said the relocation would lower its overall costs.

"MetraByte has not achieved acceptable sales growth and earnings," Keithley said. "We believe this reorganization will result in a stronger Data Acquisition Business with better customer service, more leading edge products and more opportunities for future growth in sales and earnings."
The new Data Acquisition Business would combine the MetraByte Personal Computer Plug-in Board business with the new Cleveland-based Network Measurements organization, the company said.
